Regina Zhang

  • Postdoctoral Associate, Yale UniversityRadiology & Biomedical Imaging, with Jinsong Ouyang and Xiaofeng Liu
  • Postdoctoral Researcher, University of Cambridgewith Pietro Liò
  • Ph.D. in Computer Science, The University of Hong Kongadvised by Siu-Ming Yiu

I develop AI methods for data science and biomedical informatics, with a focus on learning from graphs and time series that are noisy, incomplete, and evolving. My current work designs algorithms to forecast how Alzheimer’s pathology progresses across the brain and to advance PET tracer research.

Google Scholar (opens in a new tab) reginazhang955@gmail.com

Research agendaDirections for an independent group

My future research direction will focus on developing novel, robust, and efficient foundation models and graph neural networks for evolving graphs and time series, with rigorous validation in high-stakes applications, beginning with neurodegenerative disease.

  1. AIM 1 · FORECAST

    Forecasting disease progression on brain networks

    Forecast regional tau accumulation in Alzheimer’s disease from longitudinal PET, using brain connectivity as structure, accounting for scan quality, and producing calibrated uncertainty validated across cohorts.

  2. AIM 2 · PERSONALIZE

    Individualized models of progression

    Integrate imaging with genomic information so that forecasts reflect the individual patient rather than the population average.

  3. AIM 3 · GENERALIZE

    Reusable methods and rigorous benchmarks

    Release algorithms and benchmarks that show when robust and efficient graph learning helps, how it transfers across domains, and what it costs.
